hero.headline: Help build the 2027 festival
hero.intro: Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết returns to Elk Grove Park this February — welcoming the Year of the Goat with a free, family-centered festival weekend: carnival, lion dance, kids programming, and local live music. Vendor fees fund the essentials. Sponsors unlock the magic.
hero.subhead: Join weekly production calls, Discord, or own a director lane — we organize as a network of owners, not a stiff org chart.
hero.body: Start by showing up to production meetings. Prefer a traditional lane? Browse open director roles. Bringing a celebration vision? We’ll help you find a crew and a path to ship it. Steering Committee: Bao Thien Ngo (cPALSs) and Thuy Pham (VACOS).

steps: Email contact@eglny.com — name the role or vision you’re interested in, preferred contact method (email, text, or phone), and any other events you’re already working on this season.
We’ll follow up within a few business days — add you to the staff directory or introduce you to a visionary crew, and set a first check-in.

members.name: Bao Thien Ngo
members.title: cPALSs
members.vision: I want LNY to stay a place people show up as themselves — not a stiff volunteer org chart. Inspiration and creativity are the point: cultivate artistry and passion people can share, not bury under corporate departments or where a few people are chained to putting out fires. I gather people who own their own visions, fold calendars so busy people’s work compounds across more than one idea, and honestly name the gaps so we can help one another realize the collective dream.

members.name: Lily Tran
members.title: Lucky Wav
members.vision: If you grew up celebrating Lunar New Year, you know what it means to keep culture and tradition alive — and that each generation has its own way of expressing that. When I was asked to lead music for Elk Grove LNY, I got space to create something different. That’s how Lucky Wav was born: Lucky for blessings ahead, Wav for music, movement, and a new wave of culture. This segment is about honoring where we come from and celebrating where we’re headed — for our community in Sacramento and Elk Grove.

directorIntro.title: What is a director?
paragraphs: A director is the go-to person for one festival lane. You don't have to do every task yourself — you own the plan, coordinate vendors and volunteers, and report status to the Steering Committee. Most roles are planning now through February 2027; peak workload is the two weeks before and event weekend.
Already covered: Steering Committee — Bao Thien Ngo (cPALSs) and Thuy Pham (VACOS). They hold coalition partnership-level decision authority; every lane director is open for 2027 recruitment.

23 director roles are open across site & ops, program & experience, and outreach & partners. Member and support roles fill in behind each director. Returning 2026 volunteers are welcome to apply — nothing is assumed until confirmed on the staff directory.
notes: Prefer one accountable director per traditional lane. Multiple visionaries may share a lane as co-equals until a director coordinates them — see FAQ on Team.
Youth Culture Day (school multicultural rallies on stage) and Tết Relay Cup (open-age relay bracket on grass) are separate lanes with separate directors.
Parade is a sponsor-gated Phase 2 committee — Chair oversees Creative Director + Producer; likely cut at MVP unless a registry block funds it.
Saturday 5–8 PM headliner is sponsor unlock, not MVP baseline.
Volunteers Director owns shifts; if a critical lane stays unfilled past the steering trigger date, a contractor fallback may be approved.

faq.a: Helpful, not required. LNY 2026 runbooks and co-chairs back you up.

faq.q: What's the difference between a director and a visionary?
faq.a: A director is the accountable owner of a traditional festival lane (one preferred name on the directory). A visionary owns a celebration vision and builds a crew around it — often along the journey to the weekend, not only day-of. Multiple visionaries can share a lane as co-equals until a director coordinates them.

Generally not — these are volunteer leadership roles. We are open to contractors when a role is funded. Full transparency: if you want paid marketing or similar work, we will likely ask you to pair that with a fundraising strategy and execute it to fund the role (and any campaign spend).

We prefer one person accountable for a traditional director role on the staff directory. There may be situations where multiple visionaries live in the same lane and are treated as co-equals until we find a single director to oversee and coordinate them.

faq.q: What if my experience isn't funded yet?
faq.a: We operate as a network of owners. We put the word out when an experience is unfunded, but it is up to everyone to recruit help and spread the ask. We will create incentives so pitching in is worthwhile — gift registry blocks, sponsorship commission paths, and peer grapevine recruiting — not a single person carrying every fundraising ask.
Planning baseline ~6,000 attendees over the weekend — a family fair, not a ticketed night market. Free gate, daylight hours (11 AM – 5 PM baseline).

faq.q: I'm working on other events — can I still help with LNY?
faq.a: Yes — tell us your season commitments by email and we'll coordinate so nothing collides.

about.headline: About Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết

sections.title: Tết
paragraphs: Lunar New Year, known as Tết in Vietnamese culture, is one of the most significant and cherished celebrations in Asian communities worldwide. This ancient festival marks the beginning of the lunar calendar year and symbolizes renewal, family reunion, and hope for prosperity. For Vietnamese families, Tết represents a time to honor ancestors, strengthen family bonds, and welcome good fortune for the year ahead. Traditional celebrations include preparing special foods, decorating homes with flowers and symbols of luck, exchanging red envelopes (lì xì) for good fortune, and gathering with loved ones to reflect on the past year while embracing new beginnings.

For Vietnamese and Asian communities that fled after the Fall of Saigon following decades of war, arriving in America meant starting over in an unfamiliar land. As refugees worked to rebuild their livelihoods and establish new roots, Lunar New Year celebrations served a crucial function — providing a place of familiarity and community connection in their adopted homeland. This ancient tradition became more than just a cultural observance; it became an essential anchor that helped displaced families reorient themselves, maintain their identity, and forge bonds with fellow community members navigating similar challenges of resettlement.

sections.title: Sacramento & Elk Grove
paragraphs: Today, Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết builds on decades of cultural celebrations in the Sacramento region — from Stockton Boulevard and Florin to Elk Grove Park. The festival is a free, family-centered gathering that welcomes the whole community: carnival, lion dance, multicultural programming, and live music.

The festival is co-hosted by Community Partners Advocate of Little Saigon Sacramento (cPALSs), Vietnamese American Community of Sacramento (VACOS), and Norcal Vietnamese Chamber of Commerce (NVCC), with generous support from sponsors, donors, and volunteers.
We hope you consider supporting our culturally-oriented and community-driven festival as part of this historical moment for our community.
